exhibits.title: Two Standards, One Objective
exhibits.text:
Two banners hang facing each other. On the left, π0: 3.3 billion parameters, a PaliGemma 3B backbone with a 300M action expert inside the same transformer. On the right, SmolVLA: 0.45 billion in total, a SmolVLM-2 backbone with an action expert of about 100M in a stack of its own.

They are trying to do the same thing, and the mathematics they use to do it is IDENTICAL. Same flow-matching loss, same straight path, same Euler integration, same action chunk as the thing being refined. Nothing on this plinth is a disagreement about the objective.

What they disagree about is CONDITIONING DESIGN — how the action side gets to look at the observation.

π0 puts the expert inside the backbone's transformer and lets token type select the weights, so the two populations meet in one joint self-attention at every layer. SmolVLA keeps the expert as a separate stack that reads the backbone's features from outside, alternating cross-attention layers (actions attend to VLM features) with self-attention layers (actions attend to each other, causally).

The two banners also differ on a detail that is easy to miss and genuinely consequential: they put the robot's proprioceptive state on OPPOSITE SIDES of the bridge. That is the third plinth, and it repays a careful reading.

exhibits.title: Shared Attention, or Interleaved Cross-Attention
exhibits.text:
The bridge between the vision-language side and the action side is where these two designs actually diverge.

π0 — SHARED SELF-ATTENTION. One joint attention operation over the whole sequence, every layer. Each token computes Q, K, V with its own expert's weights, and then everything attends to everything. The action tokens see raw backbone tokens at every depth, not a summary.

SmolVLA — INTERLEAVED CROSS AND SELF ATTENTION. The expert is a separate stack with two kinds of layer alternating. A cross-attention layer lets action tokens attend to the VLM's features. A self-attention layer lets action tokens attend to each other, causally. The two never merge into a single joint operation.

The difference is not cosmetic. Under shared attention the sequence is one long joint sequence and the expert's width is tied to the backbone's stack. Under cross-attention the action sequence stays short and the expert can be sized independently — but the features are READ once per cross-attention layer rather than fused throughout.

SmolVLA's paper ablates the interleaving and finds it load-bearing. The π-family follow-ups have largely kept the shared design.

exhibits.title: The State Sits on Opposite Sides
exhibits.text:
The subtle point, and the one most worth carrying away from this chamber: the two papers put the proprioceptive state on OPPOSITE SIDES of the bridge.

SmolVLA puts it in the VLM PREFIX. A linear layer turns the state into a single token, which is concatenated with the image and text tokens before the backbone runs. The consequence is that every feature the expert later reads by cross-attention is ALREADY STATE-AWARE — the vision-language representation was computed knowing where the arm was.

π0 keeps it on the ACTION EXPERT SIDE, concatenated with the noisy action chunk. The state token is processed by the expert's weights and meets vision only through attention, in the same joint operation that carries everything else.

Both work. But they answer a real design question differently: should posture inform how the scene is PERCEIVED, or only how the scene is ACTED ON? SmolVLA says perception should be posture-conditioned. π0 keeps perception task-general and does the fusing later.

If you port code between the two and move the state token without noticing, you have changed the model's information flow, not just its plumbing.

exhibits.title: Half the Layers, Skipped
exhibits.text:
SmolVLA's economy comes from more than a smaller backbone. It also SKIPS LAYERS.

Rather than running SmolVLM-2 to its final layer and reading the top representation, it takes features from layer N = L/2 — half the depth — and never computes the rest. Half the vision-language stack simply does not run.

The bet is that the upper half of a vision-language model is largely dedicated to producing good TEXT, and a policy does not need text. Mid-stack features are already grounded, already fused, and already sufficient to condition an action expert. The paper's ablations support the choice.

π0 makes the opposite bet, running PaliGemma 3B in full and letting the action expert attend to every layer of it. Its economy comes from elsewhere — from caching, which the last chamber of this wing explains.

Two different routes to an affordable policy: skip computation you argue you do not need, or do the computation once and reuse it. They are not mutually exclusive, and the totals show what each buys — 3.3B against 0.45B.

exhibits.title: The Couriers' Ledger
exhibits.text:
π0 against SmolVLA, line by line, with the trade-offs each design accepts.

I. THE COMPARISON.

                    π0                          SmolVLA
  Total             3.3B                        0.45B
  Action expert     300M                        ~100M
  VLM               PaliGemma 3B, all layers    SmolVLM-2, LAYER SKIPPING at N = L/2
                    SigLIP + Gemma              SigLIP + SmolLM2

  State enters      ACTION EXPERT side          VLM PREFIX
                    concat with noisy chunk     linear → 1 token, concat with image+text

  Expert location   INSIDE the same transformer SEPARATE transformer stack
                    token type selects weights  reads VLM features from outside

  Bridge            SHARED SELF-ATTENTION       INTERLEAVED CROSS + SELF ATTENTION
                    one joint attention over    CA layer: actions attend to VLM features
                    all tokens                  SA layer: actions attend to each other, causal
                                                alternating, never joint

  Objective         IDENTICAL — the same flow matching loss and Euler integration

II. π0's TRADE-OFFS.
  + the expert sees RAW backbone tokens at every layer, not a pooled summary
  + the VLM's keys and values are cached across all 10 integration steps
  − one long joint sequence to attend over, and attention pays the square of length
  − the expert's width is tied to the backbone's stack
  adopted by most π-family follow-ups

III. SmolVLA's TRADE-OFFS.
  + the expert is sized independently of the VLM
  + cross-attention keeps the action sequence short
  + half the VLM layers are skipped entirely
  − features are read once per CA layer rather than fused throughout
  the interleaving is ablated as load-bearing in the paper

IV. WHAT IS SHARED, AND IT IS MOST OF IT. Both are flow-matching policies. Both refine an action chunk that is an INPUT, not an output. Both integrate with Euler over a small number of steps. Both use SigLIP as the vision encoder, π0 through PaliGemma and SmolVLA through SmolVLM-2 — the same contrastive encoder you met in the Observatory, sitting under both robots. Both normalise actions per dimension and denormalise before hardware. The disagreement is confined to conditioning design.

V. HOW TO READ THE DISAGREEMENT. The question underneath is how much of the vision-language model an action policy actually needs, and how directly it needs to reach it. π0 answers: all of it, at every layer, joined by attention. SmolVLA answers: half of it, read at intervals, with the state folded in early so the features arrive already aware of the body. Neither has been shown to dominate. Both are cheap enough to run at control rates, which was the constraint that mattered.

exhibits.title: The Portrait of Two Engineers
exhibits.subtitle: arguing about where the state belongs
exhibits.text:
"You buried the state on the action side. Your vision features have no idea where the arm is."

"They do not need to. Perception is task-general — the towel is where it is whether my elbow is up or down. I fuse posture at attention time, in every layer, and my expert reads raw tokens rather than a summary."

"And pays for one long joint sequence to do it. I put the state in the prefix, so my features come out already knowing the body. Then a hundred million parameters of expert reads them by cross-attention, on a short sequence, from half a backbone."

"Half a backbone."

"Half. Layer N = L/2. The upper half is for producing text and I am not producing text. Three point three billion against four hundred and fifty million, and the loss function is the same line of code in both repositories."

"That last part is true, at least. We disagree about wiring, not about flow matching."

exhibits.title: Two Bridges
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  P1["π0: image + text tokens"] --> P3["ONE transformer, two weight sets, 3.3B"]
  P2["π0: state token + 50 action tokens"] --> P3
  P3 --> P4["joint self-attention, every layer"]
  P4 --> P5["velocity"]
  S1["SmolVLA: image + text + STATE token"] --> S2["SmolVLM-2, stop at layer L/2"]
  S2 --> S3["VLM features, already state-aware"]
  S3 --> S4["separate expert stack, ~100M"]
  S5["SmolVLA: action tokens"] --> S4
  S4 --> S6["alternating cross-attn and causal self-attn"]
  S6 --> S7["velocity"]
exhibits.caption: The same objective reached over two different bridges. π0 runs one transformer in which token type selects the weight set, so action tokens meet image tokens in a single joint attention at every layer, and the state rides on the action side. SmolVLA folds the state into the VLM prefix so its features are already state-aware, stops the backbone halfway, and hands those features to a separate expert that alternates cross-attention with causal self-attention.
